terms.definition: Overarching steering frame for large enterprises: enterprise strategy, cross-portfolio initiatives, long-term investment planning, prioritisation across portfolios, guardrails, decision rights, transparency on results and reallocation.
terms.distinction: Our reference model, not a universal standard. The term 'Strategic Portfolio Management' is also used in the market.

terms.definition: Steers a portfolio through strategy and investment funding, Agile portfolio operations and Lean governance.
terms.distinction: Not just a delivery layer. Larger enterprises may run several LPM portfolios.
terms.variants: SAFe term; the app also explains hybrid and other flow-based delivery models.

terms.definition: Discipline for a shared economic view of technology: costs, resources, solutions, consumers, allocation and value.
terms.distinction: Distinct from budgeting, forecasting and accounting, which remain finance processes. TBM provides transparency and drivers as input.

terms.definition: Connects steering with business capabilities, product and application landscapes, platforms, dependencies, current and target states, roadmaps, lifecycles and technical risk.
terms.distinction: Distinguishes [[business-capability]], [[product]], [[application]] and [[platform]] rather than treating them as the same thing.

terms.definition: Budgeting, forecasting, accounting and capitalisation.
terms.distinction: Adjacent to technology steering, with interfaces to investment planning and to [[tbm]].

terms.definition: An intended effect at enterprise or portfolio level.
terms.distinction: Not a [[metric]]. Strategic themes are adapted at portfolio level in SAFe.

terms.definition: What the organisation must be able to do, independent of how, by whom and with what it is done. Organised hierarchically.
terms.distinction: Not an [[application]], not a [[product]], not a process.

terms.definition: A cross-portfolio bundle of investments serving an enterprise objective. Its investments may themselves span portfolios.
terms.distinction: A separate steering level only in the enterprise variant.

terms.definition: A steering unit with its own budget, value streams, strategy and governance.
terms.distinction: Not every portfolio is coupled to others; a portfolio may run without any cross-portfolio investments.

terms.definition: Generic investment and work item with a business case or benefit hypothesis. It can span portfolios: funded and delivered in several portfolios, with exactly one lead portfolio.
terms.distinction: A delivered investment is not yet a realised [[outcome]].

terms.definition: A portfolio's share in an investment: role (lead or contributing), funding share and delivering value streams.
terms.distinction: Prevents double counting when investments span portfolios.

terms.definition: A long-lived delivery organisation with its own capacity that creates value for customers or consumers. Belongs to exactly one portfolio.
terms.distinction: Not a project phase. Lean budgets fund value streams instead of projects.

terms.definition: An offering for customers or internal users with accountability for outcomes.
terms.distinction: Not an [[application]]: a product may use several applications.

terms.definition: A shared technical or business foundation used by several products.
terms.distinction: Has internal consumers; how it is funded is a separate steering question.

terms.definition: A consumable offering with a defined service promise (business or IT service).
terms.distinction: TBM technology solutions include services and products.

terms.definition: A software system that realises business capabilities and uses technologies.
terms.distinction: Not a [[product]] and not a [[business-capability]].

terms.definition: A technical component such as a database, runtime or infrastructure, with a lifecycle status.
terms.distinction: Lifecycle status (for example end-of-life) drives modernisation and risk.

terms.definition: Assignment of budget to a recipient (portfolio, value stream, initiative or platform), with guardrails.
terms.distinction: Not a [[cost-allocation]]: funding decides what may be spent, cost allocation distributes what was spent.

terms.definition: An agreed boundary within which decisions may be made in a delegated way.
terms.distinction: The specific SAFe guardrails are not yet verified against the source.

terms.definition: Actual costs grouped by cost type.
terms.distinction: TBM taxonomy layer 'Technology Cost Pool'.

terms.definition: A category of technology resources.
terms.distinction: TBM taxonomy layer 'Technology Resource Towers'.

terms.definition: A consumable solution, such as a product or service, to which costs are assigned.
terms.distinction: TBM taxonomy layer 'Technology Solutions'. Modelled in this app as product, platform or service; an application is not a solution by itself.

terms.definition: An organisational unit or user group that consumes technology solutions.
terms.distinction: TBM taxonomy layer 'Technology Consumer', called 'Business Layer' before version 5.0.

terms.definition: Distribution of actual costs from cost pools via resource towers and solutions to consumers, using drivers, including unallocated shares.
terms.distinction: Not a [[funding-allocation]] and not the same as [[chargeback]].

terms.definition: Costs that are deliberately not assigned to a consumer or an investment.
terms.distinction: A legitimate part of the model, not an error.

terms.definition: Costs are made transparent to consumers but not charged.
terms.distinction: Unlike [[chargeback]], no internal charge is made.

terms.definition: Costs are charged internally to consumers.
terms.distinction: Unlike [[showback]], consumers bear the cost economically.

terms.definition: Available capacity per value stream or team and period, split across RUN, CHANGE and investments.
terms.distinction: In flow-based models RUN and CHANGE are a capacity split, not separate budget lines.

terms.definition: Steering perspectives: operating and sustaining versus changing and building.
terms.distinction: Not the same as [[capex-opex]].

terms.definition: Accounting treatment of spending as capital or operating expenditure.
terms.distinction: An interface to finance, not a steering perspective. Lean budgets can contain both.

terms.definition: The kind of financial value: target, budget, forecast or actual.
terms.distinction: Independent of [[run-change]] and [[capex-opex]]. Values of different types are never added up.

terms.definition: A top-down orientation value, for example a cost target or cost ratio.
terms.distinction: Not an approved [[budget]], and not an outcome goal (outcomes use 'expected').

terms.definition: Approved funds per period and level (plan).
terms.distinction: Not [[actual-cost]] and not a [[target]].

terms.definition: The current expectation of a value for the period, updated on a rolling basis.
terms.distinction: Not a [[budget]]. Forecasting is a finance process with input from portfolio management and TBM.

terms.definition: Costs actually booked.
terms.distinction: Not a [[budget]] and not a [[forecast]]. Cost allocation is applied to actuals.

terms.definition: A derived difference between two value types, for example forecast versus budget.
terms.distinction: Always calculated, never stored as a base value.

terms.definition: A delivered result, for example a feature that is live.
terms.distinction: Not an [[outcome]].

terms.definition: An observable change in behaviour or results, for example adoption or handling time.
terms.distinction: Not an [[output]] and not a [[financial-benefit]].

terms.definition: An effect valued in money, such as revenue or cost avoidance.
terms.distinction: Not an [[outcome]].

terms.definition: A measurable quantity for output, outcome or benefit, with an expected and an actual value.
terms.distinction: Several investments may contribute; a change is not attributed to a single investment.

terms.definition: The expected outcome or benefit of an investment, stated so that it can be tested.
terms.distinction: The SAFe variant (epic hypothesis) is not yet verified against the source.

terms.definition: Who (role or body) decides on which type of decision at which level.
terms.distinction: Depends on the organisational scenario.

terms.definition: A cross-discipline steering task. The model uses eight of them.
terms.distinction: Not an organisational unit and not a governance body.

terms.definition: Link type: X contributes to objective or capability Y.
terms.distinction: Does not imply funding or delivery.

terms.definition: Link type: budget is assigned from X to Y.
terms.distinction: Not a cost flow.

terms.definition: Link type: actual costs flow from X to Y.
terms.distinction: Not a funding flow.

terms.definition: Link type: X builds or delivers Y.
terms.distinction: Delivery does not imply a realised outcome.

terms.definition: Link type: X depends technically on Y.
terms.distinction: A technical dependency, not an organisational one.

terms.definition: Link type: results from X inform decisions in Y.
terms.distinction: Closes the steering loop from operations and value realisation back to strategy and funding.
